issues.legal_issue: A landowner who engages a builder to construct a building and receives a specified share of the constructed area is a consumer when the arrangement does not make the landowner a co-venturer sharing control or management of the project.
material_facts: The landowner agreed to provide the land for construction of a multi-storey building and to receive 40% of the constructed area, while the builder was to receive 60%.
The builder controlled construction, and the landowner had no say in the construction or participation in the project’s business or management.
The agreement required the landowner to register some flats for purchasers of the builder, but did not provide for shared control or shared profits and losses as co-venturers.
The landowner complained of delayed construction and other deficiencies in the work.
issues.conclusion: The agreement was not a true joint venture, and the landowner was a consumer entitled to pursue the complaint under the Act. The fact that some flats were to be sold did not alter that conclusion.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(1)(d)(ii) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, as amended, a person who hires or avails of services for consideration may be a consumer, subject to the exclusion for services availed of for a commercial purpose and the self-employment explanation. Whether a purpose is commercial depends on the facts and circumstances of the case: Laxmi Engineering Works v. P.S.G. Industrial Institute (1994) 4 SCC 225; Punjab University v. Unit Trust of India (2015) 2 SCC 669. Applying Faqir Chand Gulati v. Uppal Agencies Pvt. Ltd. (2008) 10 SCC 345, a development agreement is not a true joint venture merely because the landowner and builder share constructed area or the agreement uses collaborative language. The relevant distinction is whether they share control, management, and the risks and benefits of the venture; where the builder controls construction and the landowner is entitled to a specified constructed area for consideration, the landowner avails of the builder’s service. The principles in Faqir Chand Gulati apply notwithstanding the later amendment to the definition of consumer.

rule.if: consumer_service_complaint and landowner_builder_development_agreement and builder_controls_construction and owner_receives_specified_constructed_share and not owner_shares_project_control_or_business

predicates.consumer_service_complaint: A person brings a consumer-service complaint concerning work performed by a service provider.
predicates.landowner_builder_development_agreement: A landowner agrees with a builder that the builder will develop the land and the parties will receive shares of the constructed property.
predicates.builder_controls_construction: The builder, rather than the landowner, controls the construction work.
predicates.owner_receives_specified_constructed_sha: The landowner is entitled to a specified share of the constructed area under the agreement.
predicates.owner_shares_project_control_or_business: The landowner participates with the builder in controlling or managing the project’s business.

issues.definition: When a landowner brings a consumer-service complaint under a development agreement, the landowner is a consumer if the builder controls construction, the owner receives a specified constructed share, and the owner does not share control or participation in the project’s business.

issues.legal_issue: When appellate consumer fora dismiss a complaint solely because the complainant is not a consumer and therefore do not adjudicate the merits, the matter must be remitted for merits adjudication if that status determination is erroneous.
material_facts: The District Forum had found the complainant to be a consumer and partly allowed the claims concerning delayed construction and other deficiencies.
The State Commission dismissed the claims as not maintainable because it found the complainant was not a consumer, and the National Commission affirmed that decision.
The Supreme Court held that the complainant was a consumer and did not express an opinion on the merits of the claims.
issues.conclusion: The orders of the State Commission and National Commission were set aside, and the matter was remitted to the State Commission to re-adjudicate the claims treating the complainant as a consumer.
issues.legal_principle: Where the appellate fora have disposed of a complaint on the threshold ground that the complainant is not a consumer, and that ground is erroneous, the merits remain to be adjudicated. The Supreme Court therefore set aside those orders and remitted the matter without expressing an opinion on the merits.

rule.if: appeal_from_consumer_forum_decision and appellate_forums_dismissed_complaint_only_on_consumer_status and merits_remain_unadjudicated and consumer_status_ground_is_erroneous

predicates.appeal_from_consumer_forum_decision: A party appeals from a decision in a consumer-service complaint.
predicates.appellate_forums_dismissed_complaint_onl: The appellate fora dismissed the complaint solely because they found the complainant was not a consumer.
predicates.merits_remain_unadjudicated: The appellate fora did not decide the substantive claims about the alleged deficiency in service.
predicates.consumer_status_ground_is_erroneous: The finding that the complainant was not a consumer is contrary to the facts and applicable principles.

issues.definition: If an appeal concerns a consumer complaint dismissed by appellate fora only on consumer status, the merits remain undecided, and that status ground is erroneous, the matter is remanded for merits adjudication treating the complainant as a consumer.
